title: Nothing mechanically catches OData query params nested under a dead `options` key in a `find()` call
body:
Follow-up from #4025 (the third bullet of its "建议范围"), split out rather than carried in that card's PR — see "Why this is not in that PR" below.

## The gap

`QueryParams` (`packages/types/src/data.ts`) declares its paging keys at the **top level** (`$top` / `$skip`) and carries an index signature (`[key: string]: any`). That index signature means the type system can never reject a misspelled or misplaced query key: `find(obj, { options: { $top: 100 } })` type-checks exactly as well as `find(obj, { $top: 100 })`, and the two mean completely different things — the first means nothing at all. No adapter in this repo reads `params.options` (`convertQueryParams` in `@object-ui/data-objectstack` and `ApiDataSource` both read `params.$top`), so a cap written there never reaches the wire.

Two live instances existed, both written by different people at different times:

- `object-timeline` — the whole fetch was `find(objectName, { options: { $top: 100 } })`; fixed in PR #4009 (objectstack#7137).
- `object-kanban` — `$filter` at the top level, the cap under `options`; fixed for #4025. A board over a large object fetched every row the server would return, for as long as the block existed.

Plus a harmless one in `@object-ui/fields` (primary-key equality, at most one row), spelled top-level as of the same PR.

The pattern is exactly the kind that a review will not catch twice in a row: it reads as a deliberate grouping ("query options"), it type-checks, it publishes, and the symptom (too many rows) looks like a data problem rather than a code problem.

## State right now

After the #4025 PR there are **zero live instances in the repo** — the only remaining textual matches are prose in comments and test headers describing the history. That makes this the cheapest possible moment to install the gate: it starts green with no allowlist and no debt entry.

Verified with:

```
grep -rnE 'options\s*:\s*\{[^}]*\$(top|skip|filter|orderby|select|expand)' packages apps examples --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx
```

## What to build — a decision this issue exists to make

**Option A — a `check:*` script** (the shape #4025 suggested). Consistent with the repo's other correctness gates (`check:phantom-deps`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:i18n-keys` all parse sources with `typescript`), so this one should too rather than regex over raw text: comments and test headers legitimately contain the dead spelling, and a text scan would have to strip comments approximately to avoid flagging them. Suggested AST signature, which needs no allowlist:

> an object-literal property named `options` whose initialiser is an object literal containing at least one property whose name starts with `$`

Cost: script + a pin test in `scripts/__tests__/` + a step in `ci.yml`'s type-check job (the house pattern for every gate there).

**Option B — an `object-ui/*` ESLint rule** in `eslint-rules/`, alongside `no-dynamic-import-in-test-hook` and friends. Same AST precision, plus an editor-time squiggle at the moment the mistake is typed rather than at CI, and `eslint.config.js` already carries the `error`-level ratchet convention (and `check-lint-coverage.mjs` guarantees every package runs ESLint). Cost: rule + RuleTester test.

The two are not equivalent in reach: the ESLint rule sees only linted workspace packages, while a `check:*` script chooses its own scan roots. Whoever picks this up should pick one deliberately — not both.

## Acceptance

- A newly introduced `find(obj, { options: { $top: N } })` (or any `$`-prefixed key nested under `options`) fails CI with a message that says where the key belongs.
- Existing prose mentioning the dead spelling (comments in `plugin-timeline`, `plugin-kanban`, `fields`, and the test headers) does not trip it.
- The gate ships green against `main` with no allowlist.

## Not in scope here

Any wider "unknown `QueryParams` key" gate. The index signature is deliberate (adapters accept adapter-specific params), so a general unknown-key check would be a much larger design question about tightening the type itself. This issue is the one spelling that has already cost two blocks their row caps.

## Why this is not in the #4025 PR

That card adjudicated the gate as in-scope "only if it lands as a small `check:*` script addition". By this repo's convention a new gate is a script plus a pin test plus a workflow step (or a rule plus a RuleTester test), and the mechanism choice above is a real decision with a reviewable trade-off — neither fits inside a three-line behaviour fix without making that fix harder to review. Filing it here keeps both reviewable.
